summary: Reconnaissance complete; no files written. Two findings. (1) Blocking: u18-era-baseline.json's 64-entry inventory publishes sha256(readFileSync(path,'latin1')), not sha256 of the files — 64/64 match latin1, only 22/64 match real sha256. Same defect in three published angular-factoriolab records. The era lane cannot be bound as goal item 1 requires, since the witness verifier computes real sha256 over the served root. Retained rebuild-*.manifest.txt files are raw-correct and offer a clean rebinding. (2) The font-inlining probe found an undeclared, migration-introduced, every-build fetch to fonts.googleapis.com against a consent that sets alternateHostsAllowed:false.
open_questions: Era-lane binding: bind the served era root to the raw-correct retained rebuild-2/rebuild-3.manifest.txt and issue a supersede-by-reference correction record under evidence/runs/angular-super-productivity-v2-13-15/, or re-issue the inventory with raw digests as a new u18k record? Both change what u20b/u20c bind to, so I want the ruling before writing the schema.

The latin1 digest defect also sits in evidence/runs/angular-factoriolab/{m2-era-baseline,m2-migrated-build,m2-build-parity}.json, which back a PUBLISHED vertical and are outside my file contract. Comparison conclusions stay valid (latin1 decoding is byte-injective); only the published digest values are wrong. Who owns that correction, and should the digest-writing harness be fixed centrally first?

Font locality: fonts.googleapis.com is on no allowlist (consent VL-LEGACY-CORPUS-2026-08-10 declares alternateHostsAllowed:false; allowed hosts are registry.yarnpkg.com, registry.npmjs.org, codeload.github.com, github.com), and a production build is neither acquisition nor a package-manager window. Does this need a consent amendment or a rebuild with optimization.fonts.inline disabled before the witness vertical publishes?
Published angular-tiny-translator asserts the same Angular 16 build-time Google Fonts inlining, so it likely carries the same undeclared fetch. Should that be probed as a separate unit?
